exposure: Migration (living in a household with migrants/receiving remittances)
outcome: Utilisation of maternal health services (skilled health personnel attendance at delivery, antenatal visits, postnatal checks, financial protection for delivery/prenatal/postnatal care)
Utilisation of child health services (postnatal checks, vaccinations)
cohort: The study participants were mothers aged 15-49 years who had recently given birth in Togo, categorized by whether their household had migrants.
finding: Households with migrants demonstrated significantly higher utilisation of maternal and child health services, including skilled birth assistance, antenatal visits, and postnatal checks, compared to households without migrants.
cross-section timing: Data was analyzed for mothers who had recently given birth, focusing on their recent utilization of health services.
